mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes during a tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes under these labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A double-digit year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals weakening household demand, which depresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and prompts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of such dual-shock episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.4 percentage points in a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of such triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 6-month moving averages signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of such dual-demand contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between industrial production growth (INDPRO) and S&P 500 forward returns exists: when INDPRO grows above its 3-month moving average, S&P 500 tends to rise over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 3-mo MA is followed by negative or flat S&P 500 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances over a 10-year sample.
